🇲🇽📈 <u>SUPERPESO SHRUGS OFF TRUMP'S UPDATED TARIFF</u>

Trump's updated 10% tariff on Mexico took effect this morning — and the peso went up. Mexico's currency appreciated 0.32% to 17.46 per dollar by midday, per Bloomberg data reported by El Financiero, as markets priced in the reality that USMCA-compliant exports keep crossing tariff-free. While 60 countries scramble to answer Washington's forced-labor decree, the peso is voting with its feet.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>NO COVER-UP: CDMX PROSECUTORS KEEP THE PAN'S REAL ESTATE CARTEL CASES OPEN</u>

Mexico City's prosecutor's office confirmed to the local Congress that the Cártel Inmobiliario investigations remain wide open: 59 active case files, 22 people bound over for trial and five convictions so far in the corruption network that ran illegal construction out of Benito Juárez under PAN administrations. Prosecutors say they are also securing full reparations for buyers who purchased illegally built apartments in good faith. The real estate cartel's political patrons keep waiting for the file to be closed. It is not closing.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>BRUGADA RENDERS ACCOUNTS: CDMX CLOSES OUT A CLEAN WORLD CUP</u>

Clara Brugada delivered Mexico City's final World Cup balance: an inter-institutional operation spanning security, mobility, civil protection, health and tourism moved millions of visitors through the capital. 'The World Cup is over and today we render accounts of the city's results,' the mayor said, crediting the coordinated work of every city agency. The right predicted chaos from a 4T capital hosting the planet's biggest event. The city just handed in its report card instead.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>WASHINGTON SLAPS 50+ MEXICANS WITH LARGEST-EVER CJNG SANCTIONS PACKAGE</u>

The US Treasury just designated more than 50 Mexican nationals and companies in its biggest sanctions package ever against the CJNG — from alleged command figures to tequila makers, gas traders, logging firms and clothing wholesalers. OFAC even names Juan Carlos González Valencia, 'El Pelón,' as the cartel's new leader after Mencho's death, with a $5 million State Department bounty on his head. Treasury chief Scott Bessent says the move hits 'the leadership, the drug trafficking operators and the illicit financial networks.' No Mexican court, no Mexican evidence — extraterritorial designations plus secondary-sanction threats against foreign banks.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>THE MAYOR WHO NEVER ANSWERED FOR SAMIR FLORES</u>

Temoac mayor Valentín Lavín was gunned down inside his own municipal palace — and activists warn the investigation into two political murders must not die with him. The Frente de Pueblos states Lavín 'had information and responsibility' in the killings of Samir Flores, the anti-thermoelectric organizer murdered in 2019, and defender Sandra Camacho, shot dead this March. Lavín never gave a single statement in the Samir Flores case. In Morelos, the questions outlive the mayor.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>LOZOYA BACK IN THE DOCK: COURT REVIVES AGRONITROGENADOS CASE</u>

A federal tribunal just dragged former Pemex chief Emilio Lozoya back into court. The Tercer Tribunal Colegiado unanimously denied his amparo and reactivated the Agronitrogenados case — frozen since August 2023. The numbers never stopped being obscene: Pemex paid $275 million for a fertilizer plant valued at $58 million brand new, and Lozoya allegedly pocketed $3.4 million from AHMSA in 2013. The court ruled that Ancira's reparations deal is no get-out-of-jail card for his co-defendant. The Peña Nieto era's favorite middleman is running out of road.

‍SILENCE: BMW confirms 2027 EV production in Mexico — zero US coverage July 23, 2026 | 💀 📰 BMW will assemble its Neue Klasse EVs — i3 sedan, iX3 crossover — and high-voltage batteries in San Luis Potosí from 2027. One of only four plants worldwide, backed by an €800M expansion. 🔍 US media filed dozens of tariff stories on Mexico this week. Stories on Mexico landing next-generation German EV production: zero.

NATIONAL REVIEW: The End of 'El Mayo' Is Only the Beginning July 23, 2026 | 🔴 📰 El Mayo got life plus a $15B forfeiture. National Review's verdict: "only the beginning." The playbook never updates — jail the boss, declare victory, demand the next escalation. 🇲🇽 Zambada ran Sinaloa for four decades; the cartel didn't miss a beat. Forty years of kingpin removals later, fentanyl is cheaper than ever. NR's answer: more of the same. (Paywalled — headline-level read, no quotes.) Source

‍EL PAÍS: Mexico leads Latin America's pushback against Trump's migrant crackdown July 20, 2026 | 🟢 📰 62 dead in 18 months of ICE operations — 52 in custody. 17 Mexicans, more than any other nationality. Mexico is the only country filing criminal complaints in US courts and state prosecutors' offices; Colombia's incoming president and Venezuela said nothing. 🇲🇽 Sheinbaum also took it to the UN. A rare piece that quotes Mexicans about Mexico. • "Seventeen Mexicans have died, and nothing has happened, not even the slightest apology" • Washington returned Mexico's protest letters: an attempt "to dictate the actions of U.S. government personnel"

‍LATIN TIMES: U.S., Mexico Announce Largest-Ever Financial Crackdown on Jalisco Cartel July 24, 2026 | 🟡 📰 Treasury's largest CJNG action ever: 55 targets — 39 people, 16 companies spanning fuel, tequila, agriculture, construction, furniture. Five months after El Mencho was killed, the cartel has a new boss and OFAC has a new list. 🔍 Two weeks ago ICG reported the crackdown hasn't dented fentanyl flows. Nobody asked Bessent about that. • "the resources it uses to traffic fentanyl, terrorize communities, and threaten American lives"
